pull.title: iwyu: Fix warnings in `src/test/fuzz` and treat them as errors
pull.body:
This PR continues the ongoing effort to enforce IWYU warnings.

See [Developer Notes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/developer-notes.md#using-iwyu).

Based on ~https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36805 and~ https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36807.

<sub>Task `Alpine (musl)`: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/42513074263/job/128830134615</sub>
<sub>LLM reason (✨ experimental): CI failed during compilation: `headerssync.cpp` has missing declarations/includes, causing incomplete `CBlockIndex` and undefined symbols.</sub>

<details><summary>Hints</summary>

Try to run the tests locally, according to the documentation. However, a CI failure may still
happen due to a number of reasons, for example:

* Possibly due to a silent merge conflict (the changes in this pull request being
incompatible with the current code in the target branch). If so, make sure to rebase on the latest
commit of the target branch.

* A sanitizer issue, which can only be found by compiling with the sanitizer and running the
  affected test.

* An intermittent issue.

Leave a comment here, if you need help tracking down a confusing failure.

</details>

> Also, I am unsure how to review the non-fuzz header changes? How do I know they are enforced by iwyu?

The changes in non-fuzz headers are enforced by IWYU because, due to the stem name coincidence, it considers them associated headers of the corresponding fuzz sources. For example, `src/test/fuzz/protocol.cpp` and `src/protocol.h`. However, they are not, because the fuzz sources contain no definitions for any declarations from those headers.

This, in turn, requires adding includes to some non-fuzz sources for headers that were previously included transitively.

> I think it would be easier if the header changes are addition-only for now?

I'm going to split out the non-fuzz changes so that they can be reviewed separately.

refactor: Introduce `node/node_id.h` header

Two identical declarations of `NodeId` make it ambiguous for static
tools such as IWYU which header should provide the symbol. Move the
declaration into a header of its own.

`net.h` re-exports it, since `NodeId` is part of its interface.
